requirements.text: An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED PCB/lamp ESA for presence of the R10 approval mark.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA that, if approved separately under R10, must carry the approval mark.

requirements.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.test_case: Verify mark location against the approval communication form.
requirements.why: Defines where the ESA approval mark must be placed on the product.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the mark for the circled E and the country number.
requirements.why: Mandatory content of the mark carried by the ESA.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the mark for '10R-' followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.
requirements.why: Mandatory content and layout of the mark carried by the ESA.

requirements.text: The approval mark affixed to the ESA shall have a dimension a of 6 mm min, as shown in the model approval marks.
requirements.test_case: Measure the circle/character dimension 'a' of the mark on the ESA (≥ 6 mm).
requirements.why: Minimum size of the approval mark the ESA must carry.

requirements.text: Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check that the mark is present on the ESA, even if hidden when installed.
requirements.why: Defines permitted mark placement on the PCB inside the lamp.

requirements.text: The ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED PCB EMC design and confirm compliance through the ESA tests of 6.5 to 6.9.
requirements.why: The rear lamp LED PCB is an ESA fitted to an M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 7, Annex 8 and Annex 10 emission tests on the lamp ESA.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA subject to R10 ESA emission testing.

requirements.text: The ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 9 and Annex 10 immunity tests on the lamp ESA.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA subject to R10 ESA immunity testing.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
requirements.test_case: Perform the broadband emission measurement per Annex 7 (CISPR 25 ALSE).
requirements.why: Defines the broadband emission test that the LED PCB ESA must pass.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6), and constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 7 broadband scan from 30 to 75 MHz and compare readings to the limit line.
requirements.why: Broadband emission limit applicable to the LED PCB ESA. [merged]

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all characteristic broadband readings are below the limit line.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for ESA broadband emissions.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform the narrowband emission measurement per Annex 8 with an average detector.
requirements.why: Defines the narrowband emission test that the LED PCB ESA must pass.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7), and constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 narrowband scan from 30 to 75 MHz and compare readings to the limit line.
requirements.why: Narrowband emission limit applicable to the LED PCB ESA. [merged]

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all characteristic narrowband readings are below the limit line.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for ESA narrowband emissions.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances of the ESA representative of its type on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure transient emissions on the lamp supply lines per ISO 7637-2.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is supplied from the 12/24 V vehicle supply lines.

requirements.text: For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA shall be +75 V.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the positive transient peak measured per ISO 7637-2 is ≤ +75 V.
requirements.why: Transient emission limit for an ESA intended for a 12 V M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity tests per ISO 11452 methods covering 20 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: Radiated immunity test for the LED PCB ESA.

requirements.text: For stripline testing, the ESA shall be tested with a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-5 stripline test at 60 V/m.
requirements.why: Table 2a immunity severity applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: For reverberation chamber testing, the ESA shall be tested with a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-11 reverberation test at 21 V/m.
requirements.why: Table 2a immunity severity applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: For stripline testing, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range shall be 50 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the stripline field never falls below 50 V/m.
requirements.why: Table 2b minimum immunity level applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: For TEM cell testing, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency range shall be 62,5 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the TEM cell field never falls below 62,5 V/m.
requirements.why: Table 2b minimum immunity level applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: For ALSE testing, the minimum test level over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range shall be 8 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the ALSE field never falls below 8 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: Table 2b minimum immunity level applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: For reverberation chamber testing, the minimum test level over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range shall be 18 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the reverberation field never falls below 18 V/m.
requirements.why: Table 2b minimum immunity level applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the "immunity related functions" of the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop and rear position lamp outputs during radiated immunity tests for any switch-off or flicker.
requirements.why: Pass criterion for ESA radiated immunity; lamp operation is an immunity related function.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses and the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines.
requirements.why: Conducted transient immunity requirement for the LED PCB ESA.

requirements.text: The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate the lamp's behaviour under the starting profile against the ISO 16750-1 classes.
requirements.why: Defines the pass criteria for the starting profile test.

requirements.text: Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate the lamp's behaviour after each pulse against the ISO 7637-1 FPSC classes.
requirements.why: Defines the pass criteria for the transient pulse tests.

requirements.text: For the starting profile, the ESA shall be tested at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems) with 10 pulses, meeting functional status B for immunity related functions of an ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESA, and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 level II starting profile pulses and check the functional status.
requirements.why: Table 3a row applicable to the ESA where starting profile applies.

requirements.text: The starting profile is only applicable to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.
requirements.test_case: Determine applicability from the intended vehicle application and apply the starting profile if applicable.
requirements.why: Defines the condition for applying the starting profile to the ESA.

requirements.text: For test pulse 1, the ESA shall be tested at -75 V (12 V system) / -450 V (24 V system) with 500 pulses, meeting FPSC III for functions related and not related to immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 500 pulses of ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 and verify status III.
requirements.why: Table 3b row applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall be tested at +37 V (12 V and 24 V system) with 500 pulses, meeting FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 500 pulses of pulse 2a and verify the lamp functions are unaffected (status I).
requirements.why: Table 3b row applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall be tested at +10 V (12 V system) / +20 V (24 V system) with 10 pulses, meeting FPSC II for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 pulses of pulse 2b and verify status II.
requirements.why: Table 3b row applicable to the ESA.

requirements.text: Where an ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and with Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Review the PCB schematic for oscillators or switching drivers above 9 kHz.
requirements.why: Exception that may remove narrowband testing for the LED PCB.

requirements.text: ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Assess whether the lamp functions are immunity related functions.
requirements.why: Exception that determines whether radiated immunity testing applies to the ESA.

requirements.text: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review the PCB circuit for switches or inductive loads.
requirements.why: Exception that determines whether transient emission testing applies to the ESA.

requirements.text: The ESA approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
requirements.test_case: Perform the paragraph 6 ESA EMC tests on production samples and compare the results with the type-approval results.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA approved under R10, so series production must match the approved type.

requirements.text: Production ESAs shall conform to the data contained in the communication form for type approval set out in Annex 3B to this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Compare the production ESA configuration and test data with the Annex 3B communication form.
requirements.why: Conformity of the LED PCB is checked against its approval communication data.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, the broadband electromagnetic radiated emission levels measured shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1. (62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band, measured according to Annex 7).
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband emissions of a series sample per Annex 7 and check the result is at most limit + 4 dB.
requirements.why: This is the CoP emission tolerance for a production ESA such as the LED driver PCB.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform Annex 9 radiated immunity tests on a series sample at 80 % of the Table 2a/2b levels and monitor lamp function for degradation.
requirements.why: This is the CoP radiated immunity criterion for a production ESA.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is being verified, the component shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 7637-2 pulses and the ISO 16750-2 starting profile at the Table 3a/3b levels to a series sample and check the functional status classification.
requirements.why: This is the CoP conducted immunity criterion for the production LED PCB.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is being verified, the component shall not exceed the conducted emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. (+75 V / -100 V for 12 V systems; +150 V / -450 V for 24 V systems).
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions of a series sample per ISO 7637-2 and compare them with the Table 1 limits.
requirements.why: This is the CoP conducted emission limit for the production ESA.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Check that the ESA broadband emission test report references CISPR 25.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA whose broadband emissions are measured by this method for §6.5.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband emission test.
requirements.test_case: Operate the LED PCB with all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) energised at maximum load during the emission scan.
requirements.why: Defines the operating state the lamp ESA must be in for compliance.

requirements.text: For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Perform the radiated emission test in an ALSE per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is not a charging ESA, so the ALSE CISPR 25 set-up applies.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply to the ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan emissions over 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare against the §6.5.2.1 limits.
requirements.why: Sets the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must meet the limits.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission test shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC test plan and report to confirm the narrowband emission test follows CISPR 25.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA, and its narrowband emission compliance under §6.6 is assessed with this method.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
requirements.test_case: Verify the LED PCB is powered with all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) active at maximum load during the measurement.
requirements.why: This defines the operating state the lamp ESA must be in when its emissions are qualified.

requirements.text: The ESA narrowband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report for an ALSE set-up per CISPR 25 clause 6.4.
requirements.why: This sets the test arrangement under which the lamp ESA must meet the limits.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan the radiated emissions of the LED PCB from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare them against the limit line.
requirements.why: This sets the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must meet the narrowband limits.

requirements.text: The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the test methods (absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5, reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11), provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex.
requirements.test_case: Review the immunity test plan and reports to confirm the chosen methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA whose radiated immunity must be demonstrated over the full frequency range.

requirements.text: The frequency range and general test conditions for the ESA immunity tests shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Check that the test reports reference ISO 11452-1 for frequency range and general conditions.
requirements.why: Sets the conditions under which the ESA's immunity is assessed.

requirements.text: The test conditions for the ESA shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the test conditions in the report conform to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.why: Constrains the conditions under which the lamp ESA must pass.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
requirements.test_case: During immunity testing, operate the LED functions (rear position, stop, reversing) in normal operation and monitor them.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA must remain functional while operating normally under exposure.

requirements.text: Immunity measurements on the ESA shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that the test sweep covers 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 step sizes.
requirements.why: Defines the frequency range over which the ESA must be immune.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Check the generator settings in the report for 20 to 400 MHz.
requirements.why: Defines the disturbance the ESA must withstand in this band.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Check the pulse modulation settings in the report for 2,700 to 3,100 MHz.
requirements.why: Defines the disturbance the ESA must withstand in this band.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check the pulse modulation settings in the report for 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: Defines the disturbance the ESA must withstand in these bands.

requirements.text: The ESA shall meet the requirements of this Annex throughout the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz at the intervals specified in ISO 11452-1, or at the reduced set of spot frequencies where the Technical Service chooses them on the basis of accredited laboratory data.
requirements.test_case: Perform the immunity test at the ISO 11452-1 intervals or the selected spot frequencies and confirm there is no malfunction.
requirements.why: The ESA must pass at all tested frequencies.

requirements.text: Where TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell.
requirements.test_case: Review the TEM cell test report for ISO 11452-3 compliance and the coupling orientation.
requirements.why: Test condition for ESA immunity if this method is selected.

requirements.text: Where bulk current injection testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, either with the substitution method and the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or with the closed loop method and the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Verify the BCI method and probe distance in the test report.
requirements.why: Test condition for ESA immunity if this method is selected.

requirements.text: Where stripline testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
requirements.test_case: Review the stripline test report for ISO 11452-5 compliance.
requirements.why: Test condition for ESA immunity if this method is selected.

requirements.text: Where the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
requirements.test_case: Review the reverberation chamber test report for ISO 11452-11 compliance.
requirements.why: Test condition for ESA immunity if this method is selected.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
requirements.test_case: Perform ISO 7637-2 and ISO 16750-2 conducted transient immunity tests on the lamp PCB supply lines and verify correct function.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA connected to the 12/24 V vehicle supply.

requirements.text: The ESA shall limit the conducted transients it emits onto the vehicle power supply.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions on the supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare with the limits.
requirements.why: The lamp PCB switches loads on the vehicle supply and can generate transients.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 to the lamp supply and connected lines and check functional status.
requirements.why: Immunity to pulse 1 is required for ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines.

requirements.text: Where the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor), the ESA is not subject to the starting profile.
requirements.test_case: Check the ESA's intended vehicle application to decide whether the starting profile test applies.
requirements.why: This exemption determines whether the starting profile test applies to the lamp PCB.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Measure transient emissions of the lamp PCB per ISO 7637-2 on the supply and connected lines.
requirements.why: The lamp PCB's conducted transient emissions must be verified on the vehicle supply.

requirements.text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the housing/lens drawing and sample for a marking area large enough for all required markings.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is a type-approved R148 device that must carry markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually check legibility and perform a rub/indelibility test on the markings.
requirements.why: Applies to all markings on the lamp.

requirements.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimension "a" of the approval mark on the tooling/sample.
requirements.why: Sizing rule for the approval mark the lamp carries.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and country number.
requirements.why: Defines the content of the approval marking on the lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4-6 digit sequential number matching the approval.
requirements.why: Required content of the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Check that the sequential number is adjacent to the circled E mark.
requirements.why: Placement rule for the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4 (R1 or R2 for the rear position lamp, S1 or S2 for the stop lamp, AR for the reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols R1/R2, S1/S2 and AR.
requirements.why: The lamp contains rear position, stop and reversing functions.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" followed by the series digits (e.g. 01).
requirements.why: Required content of the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: For a handed rear lamp, check presence of the horizontal arrow in the marking.
requirements.why: Rear lamps are typically handed (left/right) and must show mounting side.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check arrow direction on the marking relative to the vehicle side.
requirements.why: Product includes a rear position lamp.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: If the reversing lamp is approved with reduced distribution for a pair, check outward arrow direction.
requirements.why: Product includes a reversing lamp (visible to 45° outboard).

requirements.text: If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
requirements.test_case: Check the marking for "D" next to the function symbol if approved as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
requirements.why: Conditional marking for the lamp's signalling functions.

requirements.text: If applicable, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
requirements.test_case: Check the marking for "Y" next to the function symbol if part of an interdependent lamp system.
requirements.why: Conditional marking for the lamp's signalling functions.

requirements.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: If approved with reduced distribution (mounting height ≤ 750 mm), check for the downward vertical arrow symbol.
requirements.why: Rear position and stop lamps may be approved with reduced light distribution.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect sample for the approval marking.
requirements.why: Direct marking obligation on the lamp.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.
requirements.why: Direct marking obligation on the lamp.

requirements.text: Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable light sources are used, check for light source category marking.
requirements.why: Light source replaceability to be confirmed; applies if replaceable sources are used.

requirements.text: Where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), the lamp shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
requirements.test_case: If approved for LED substitute light sources, check for their category marking.
requirements.why: Conditional marking depending on light source approval.

requirements.text: Lamps with non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for rated voltage or voltage range marking.
requirements.why: The lamp uses PCB-mounted non-replaceable LED light sources.

requirements.text: Lamps with an electronic light source control gear shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: If the PCB includes control gear, check rated voltage marking.
requirements.why: The LED PCB carries drive electronics.

requirements.text: Lamps with a variable luminous intensity control shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: If R2/S2 variable intensity, check rated voltage marking.
requirements.why: Conditional on variable intensity functions.

requirements.text: Lamps with a secondary operating mode shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: If a secondary operating mode exists, check rated voltage marking.
requirements.why: Conditional on secondary operating mode.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect any replaceable module for the applicant's trade name or mark.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules are replaceable (to be confirmed).

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1.
requirements.test_case: Inspect module for 'MD' + approval mark identification code.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules are replaceable.

requirements.text: In case several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
requirements.test_case: Check that each non-identical module code has distinguishing additional characters.
requirements.why: Applies if several different replaceable modules are used.

requirements.text: The approval mark in the module identification code and the approval mark on the lamp shall be from the same applicant.
requirements.test_case: Compare module and lamp approval marks for the same applicant.
requirements.why: Applies if replaceable modules are used.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect module for rated voltage marking.
requirements.why: Applies if replaceable modules are used.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
requirements.test_case: Inspect lamp for the module identification code.
requirements.why: Applies if replaceable modules are used.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect lamp for rated voltage marking.
requirements.why: Applies if replaceable modules are used.

requirements.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: If an external control gear is used, inspect it for ID number and manufacturer name.
requirements.why: Conditional on external control electronics for the LED lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
requirements.test_case: Verify the marking location is on the lens or a part permanently joined to it.
requirements.why: Location rule for the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Check visibility of the marking with the lamp installed on the vehicle or with the boot lid opened.
requirements.why: Visibility rule for the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: If the outer lens of the device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: If the lens is detachable, inspect both lens and housing for approval markings.
requirements.why: Product has an outer lens attached to a housing.

requirements.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: If a common lens covers several devices, check each main body carries only its own function markings.
requirements.why: Product's outer lens may be shared across devices.

requirements.text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for presence of these markings.
requirements.why: Location rule for markings the lamp carries.

requirements.text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable modules are used, inspect the module itself for its markings.
requirements.why: Applies if replaceable modules are used.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps complying with several UN Regulations, it shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: With the lamp installed, verify the single approval mark is visible.
requirements.why: Rear lamp groups R148 lamps and an R150 retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Check that no light-transmitting part can be removed without removing the approval mark.
requirements.why: Applies to the grouped rear lamp assembly if a single mark is used.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the single approval mark components against the minimum sizes of R148 and R150.
requirements.why: Applies to the grouped lamp's single approval mark.

requirements.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' (and the Annexes referenced therein) of UN Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply to the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Review the lamp design against the applicable UN R48 section 5 and 6 provisions that are verifiable at lamp level.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is intended for M1 vehicles, so the R48 installation provisions are applied at lamp approval.

requirements.text: The requirements pertinent to each lamp (rear position, stop, reversing) and to the category of vehicle (M1) on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the R48 provisions for each function and for M1 vehicles that are verifiable at lamp approval, e.g. visibility angles and logos.
requirements.why: Each function of the combination lamp has to meet its pertinent installation-derived requirements.

requirements.text: The lamps must be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Run a vibration test on the mounted lamp, then re-check its photometry, colour, aim and fastener integrity.
requirements.why: This is a general construction requirement covering the housing, fasteners, PCB and optics.

requirements.text: In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source), with a note made within the communication document.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED circuitry to confirm the rear position and stop functions use separate light sources.
requirements.why: The product has a rear position lamp and a stop lamp that may share LED light sources (reciprocal incorporation).

requirements.text: Alternatively, in the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, the lamp shall be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps, with a note made within the communication document.
requirements.test_case: Verify that a failure signal output exists and that the communication form records the tell-tale restriction.
requirements.why: This is the alternative compliance route for a reciprocally incorporated rear position/stop lamp.

requirements.text: Where a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function), only one manufacturer logo shall be incorporated and all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation shall be fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Inspect for logos; if present, check there is only one and re-verify the photometry of that function.
requirements.why: This is a conditional design constraint on the lens and reflector if a logo is used.

requirements.text: Where a logo is incorporated, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo content against the vehicle manufacturer brand.
requirements.why: This is a conditional design restriction on the lamp logo.

requirements.text: Where a logo is incorporated, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected logo area in the reference-axis direction and confirm it is ≤ 100 cm2.
requirements.why: This is a dimensional limit on a logo, if one is fitted.

requirements.text: Stop lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the stop lamp apparent surface for any logo.
requirements.why: The product includes a stop lamp.

requirements.text: Reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the reversing lamp apparent surface and lens window for any logo.
requirements.why: The product includes a reversing lamp.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3, and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.
requirements.test_case: Disable each LED (group) in turn and measure the light distribution against the minima; measure with all LEDs lit against the maxima.
requirements.why: The rear position, stop and reversing functions use multiple LED light sources.

requirements.text: Alternatively, in case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in UN R48 shall be produced, with a note in the communication form that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
requirements.test_case: Simulate an LED failure and verify that the failure signal output is generated.
requirements.why: This is the alternative failure provision for the multi-LED functions.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided no restriction on use is made at the time of application), and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the light sources and confirm they are non-replaceable LEDs, light source modules or approved replaceable sources.
requirements.why: This restricts the light-source types allowed on the LED PCB lamp.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to insert the light source in incorrect orientations.
requirements.why: This applies if light-source replaceability is confirmed (stated as to be confirmed).

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061 (holder data sheet of the category prescribed, and of the LED substitute category where also prescribed).
requirements.test_case: Gauge the holder against the IEC 60061 data sheet.
requirements.why: This applies if replaceable light sources are used.

requirements.text: Light signalling devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated and conducted emission tests on the LED PCB/lamp.
requirements.why: The lamp contains an electronic LED PCB (ESA).

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to fit the module in wrong positions or orientations.
requirements.why: This applies if the LED modules are replaceable light source modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt to remove the module by hand without tools.
requirements.why: This is a conditional design requirement for replaceable LED modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module construction for tamper resistance.
requirements.why: This is a conditional design requirement for replaceable LED modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.
requirements.test_case: Check that the module interface does not accept standard approved light sources.
requirements.why: This is a conditional design requirement for replaceable LED modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module shall not be interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to swap modules between the rear position, stop and reversing positions.
requirements.why: This applies because the lamp housing contains several functions with different modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Replace the module with another of the same code and repeat the photometric measurements.
requirements.why: This is a conditional photometric requirement for replaceable LED modules.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be 13.5 V for 12 Volt-Systems (6.75 V for 6 Volt-Systems, 28 V for 24 Volt-Systems).
requirements.test_case: Supply the lamp at 13.5 V (12 V system) during the photometric and colorimetric tests.
requirements.why: This defines the supply condition under which the lamp must comply.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the HV intensity of the rear position, stop and reversing functions on both samples.
requirements.why: This is the core photometric minimum for each lamp function.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to confirm that the maximum intensity is not exceeded anywhere.
requirements.why: This is the photometric maximum for each lamp function.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in paragraph 5 by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure of Annex 3 for each direction, or not less than the intensity value specified in the pertinent Annex 3 figure for each direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure at all Annex 3 grid points and compare against the percentage or cd values.
requirements.why: This is the light distribution requirement for each function.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity throughout the Annex 2 geometric visibility angles for the rear position and stop lamps.
requirements.why: This sets the geometric visibility minimum for the signalling functions.

requirements.text: The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Check the uniformity of intensity between grid points per Annex 3.
requirements.why: This is the uniformity criterion for the light distribution.

requirements.text: Where the additional test is requested to verify visibility of white light towards the rear / red light towards the front, the maximum intensity in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard horizontally and -2.5° to +5° vertically shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity in the 165°–180° outboard field and confirm it is ≤ 0.25 cd.
requirements.why: This is an optional verification relevant to the white reversing lamp emitting towards the rear.

requirements.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Sweep the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities remain within the paragraph 5 range.
requirements.why: This applies if the lamp functions use variable intensity control.

requirements.text: For variable intensity systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 under night-time conditions.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity under night-time mode against the steady maximum.
requirements.why: This is a conditional limit for variable intensity lamps.

requirements.text: For other variable intensity systems, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 under standard conditions (good visibility MOR > 2,000 m and clean lens).
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity under standard conditions against the steady maximum.
requirements.why: This is a conditional limit for variable intensity lamps.

requirements.text: If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, the ratio between the luminous intensities of the two lamps turned on simultaneously and the rear position lamp turned on alone shall be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by ±5° V and ±10° H of the light distribution table.
requirements.test_case: Measure the combined and rear-position-only intensities across ±10° H / ±5° V and compute the ratio.
requirements.why: The product combines a rear position lamp and a stop lamp, possibly reciprocally incorporated.

requirements.text: If one or both of the reciprocally incorporated rear position and stop lamps contain more than one light source and are considered as a single lamp, the values for the 5:1 ratio shall be those obtained with all sources in operation.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ratio measurement with all LEDs lit.
requirements.why: The functions use multiple LED light sources.

requirements.text: The luminous intensities shall comply when tested according to Annex 8 (for LED: after 1 minute and after 30 minutes or photometric stability for the rear position and stop lamps; after 1 minute and after 10 minutes for the reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensities at the Annex 8 time points and check them against the minima and maxima.
requirements.why: This defines the time-dependent photometric compliance of the LED functions.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3 and shall comply with the colour requirements of the function, applying the test procedure of paragraph 4.8.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity at grid points for red (rear position, stop) and white (reversing).
requirements.why: The red lens and the white reversing window define the emitted colours.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Visually and colorimetrically inspect beyond the grid for sharp colour changes.
requirements.why: This is a colorimetric uniformity requirement for each function.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against Table 4 values.
requirements.why: P-01 is a rear position lamp and must meet the Table 4 photometric requirements.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (a)).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity on the reference axis and verify it is at least 4 cd.
requirements.why: Drawing states 4 to 17 cd on axis, corresponding to category R1.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp of category R1 (steady), when used as a single lamp, shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7∙10^1 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
requirements.test_case: Measure maximum luminous intensity over the light distribution and verify it does not exceed 17 cd.
requirements.why: Maximum intensity limit for the R1 rear position lamp.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp of category R1 is marked "D" (paragraph 3.3.2.5.2.), its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 8.5∙10^0 cd.
requirements.test_case: For a lamp marked D, measure maximum intensity and verify it does not exceed 8.5 cd.
requirements.why: Conditional limit applying if the lamp is approved for use as part of a pair (marked D).

requirements.text: The rear position lamp of category R1 shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (c)).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities at the grid points of Figure A3-I and compare with required percentages.
requirements.why: Standard light distribution required for the R1 rear position lamp.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the rear position lamp of category R1 shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (d)).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity throughout the Table A2-1 geometric visibility field and verify at least 0.05 cd.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility minimum intensity applies to the rear position lamp.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: If reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, verify intensities below 5° down do not exceed 60 cd.
requirements.why: Exception relevant because the rear lamp also contains a stop lamp function.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Simulate light source failure and verify behaviour per paragraph 4.6.
requirements.why: Failure provisions apply to the LED-based rear position lamp.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates and verify they lie within the red boundaries.
requirements.why: Colour requirement for the rear position lamp emitted through the red outer lens.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Photometric goniometer measurement of both samples against Table 7 values for the declared category.
requirements.why: Stop lamp function P-02 must meet the Table 7 luminous intensity requirements.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity on the axis shall be 60 cd (6.0∙10^1 cd).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at H-V and confirm it is ≥ 60 cd.
requirements.why: Stop lamp of M1 rear lamp is category S1 (steady), with drawing stating 60 to 185 cd on axis.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady) used as a single lamp, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 260 cd (2.60∙10^2 cd).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity over the light distribution and confirm the maximum is ≤ 260 cd.
requirements.why: Maximum intensity limit for the S1 stop lamp.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady) marked "D", the maximum luminous intensity shall be 130 cd (1.30∙10^2 cd).
requirements.test_case: If the lamp is marked "D", measure the maximum luminous intensity and confirm it is ≤ 130 cd.
requirements.why: Applies if the S1 stop lamp is approved as one of a pair marked "D".

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the grid points of Figure A3-I and compare with the required percentages of the minimum.
requirements.why: Light distribution requirement for the S1 stop lamp.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the angles of geometric visibility shall be as defined in Table A2-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the apparent surface is unobstructed and visible over the Table A2-1 angles.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility requirement for the S1 stop lamp.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall be 0.3 cd (3∙10^-1 cd).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the boundary directions of the geometric visibility field and confirm it is ≥ 0.3 cd.
requirements.why: Minimum intensity within the visibility field per Table 7 for the S1 stop lamp.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Simulate light source failure and verify compliance with paragraph 4.6.
requirements.why: Failure provisions apply to the LED stop lamp function.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the emitted light and confirm they are within the red boundaries.
requirements.why: Colour requirement for the stop lamp function.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 10.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against Table 10 values.
requirements.why: Product has a reversing lamp function (P-03) subject to R148 photometry.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10^1 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a)).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at reference axis and check ≥ 80 cd.
requirements.why: Minimum intensity limit for AR reversing lamp from Table 10.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the H-plane, 6.00∙10^2 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D, and 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b)).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan in and above the H-plane, check max ≤ 300 cd.
requirements.why: Maximum intensity limit above H-plane for AR from Table 10. [merged]

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(c)).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities at Figure A3-V grid points and compare with required percentages.
requirements.why: Standard light distribution requirement for AR from Table 10.

requirements.text: Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, where a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied.
requirements.test_case: For pair-only lamps, measure at 30° inwards and check ≥ 25 cd.
requirements.why: Conditional alternative photometric requirement applicable if lamp is approved for pair-only installation.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Verify failure behaviour of the LED reversing lamp per paragraph 4.6 (e.g. failure simulation).
requirements.why: Failure provisions apply to the reversing lamp function.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates of the reversing lamp through the outer lens window and check within white limits.
requirements.why: Reversing lamp must emit white light; relevant given red-tinted outer lens.

requirements.text: The lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Compare production samples against the approved type documentation and test results.
requirements.why: General conformity-of-production obligation applying to every approved lamp of this product.

requirements.text: No measured photometric value of a production lamp shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at all Annex 3 test points on random production lamps and check deviation is not more than 20 per cent unfavourable.
requirements.why: CoP photometric tolerance applies to the rear position, stop and reversing lamp intensities.

requirements.text: For required minimum values throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured value shall correspond to at least: for 7∙10^-1 cd: 5∙10^-1 cd (20 per cent equivalent) and 3∙10^-1 cd (30 per cent equivalent); for 3∙10^-1 cd: 2∙10^-1 cd (20 per cent) and 1∙10^-1 cd (30 per cent); for 5∙10^-2 cd: 3∙10^-2 cd (20 per cent) and 2∙10^-2 cd (30 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement at the relevant field points of production samples.
requirements.why: Table 12 row defining CoP minimum values for low-intensity field points. [merged]

requirements.text: The angles of geometric visibility shown in the arrangements are correct for lamps to be mounted on the right side of the vehicle; for lamps mounted on the left side, the inboard/outboard angles shall be applied mirror-symmetrically.
requirements.test_case: Check the goniometric visibility verification uses the correct side (left/right) orientation of the lamp as mounted.
requirements.why: Defines the orientation in which the rear lamp visibility angles must be met for each side variant.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the lamp drawing/goniometer that the apparent surface is visible from 45° inboard to 80° outboard.
requirements.why: P-01 is a rear position lamp of class R1/R2 subject to Table A2-1.

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard and 80° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify geometric visibility below the H-plane down to 20° inboard / 80° outboard for the intended mounting height below 750 mm.
requirements.why: Rear lamps on M1 vehicles are typically mounted below 750 mm, triggering note a.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility of the apparent surface at 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Vertical visibility row for rear position lamps in Table A2-1.

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 15° above and 5° below.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility at 15° up / 5° down for the low-mounted installation.
requirements.why: Note b applies to the rear position lamp when mounted below 750 mm on the M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard.
requirements.test_case: Verify on goniometer/CAD that the stop lamp apparent surface is visible from 45° inboard to 45° outboard.
requirements.why: P-02 is a stop lamp of class S1/S2 subject to Table A2-1.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility of the stop lamp apparent surface at 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Vertical visibility row for stop lamps in Table A2-1.

requirements.text: For an optional stop lamp (S1, S2) to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 5° above and 15° below.
requirements.test_case: If installed above 2,100 mm as an optional lamp, verify visibility at 5° up / 15° down.
requirements.why: Conditional case (note c) for the stop lamp row.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° if it is 750 mm or less.
requirements.why: Conditional photometric verification range for the rear position lamp function present in the product.

requirements.text: Where the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° if it is 750 mm or less.
requirements.why: Conditional photometric verification range for the stop lamp function present in the product.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light pattern should be substantially uniform. The light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value, as a percentage, shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.
requirements.test_case: Scan intensity between grid points and verify each value is at least the lowest surrounding grid minimum.
requirements.why: Uniformity requirement applying to the rear position and stop lamp distributions.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps, if visual examination appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the reversing lamp beam and, if local variations are seen, measure between the measurement directions against the 50 % criterion.
requirements.why: Local variation limit for the reversing lamp function present in the product.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I. The values give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Table 3.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the rear position lamp at all Figure A3-I points.
requirements.why: Standard light distribution applicable to the rear position lamp.

requirements.text: The stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I. The values give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the stop lamp at all Figure A3-I points.
requirements.why: Standard light distribution applicable to the stop lamp (60 cd minimum on axis, i.e. S1).

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall emit at least the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference. H = 0° and V = 0° correspond to the axis of reference.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing lamp at all Figure A3-V points against the cd minima.
requirements.why: Standard light distribution applicable to the reversing lamp.

requirements.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied if the differences of the mass-produced rear lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Dimensionally inspect production lamps against the approved type drawings and check deviations stay within manufacturing tolerances.
requirements.why: CoP mechanical/geometric criterion applies to every mass-produced lamp of the approved type.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performances, the mass-produced lamps shall meet the photometric requirements when any lamp chosen at random is tested according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation, so that their conformity is not contested.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of randomly chosen production lamps per paragraph 4.8 and compare with Annex 3 minimum and maximum values for each function.
requirements.why: Production rear position, stop and reversing lamps must keep the approved photometric performance.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by the mass-produced lamp (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity inside the Annex 3 light distribution field of each function on production samples, with the lamp's own non-replaceable light sources, and check it against the colour limits.
requirements.why: Colour of the emitted light (outer lens and LEDs) must remain compliant in production.

requirements.text: The sampled lamp shall meet the photometric minimum values at the points listed in Annex 3 and the required chromaticity coordinates.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at all Annex 3 grid points for each function and measure the chromaticity coordinates on CoP samples.
requirements.why: Defines the photometric and colorimetric characteristics that production lamps are verified against.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only (LED), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity distribution at 1 min and 10 min of operation, or calculate it by HV ratio from the stabilised distribution, and compare with min/max limits.
requirements.why: The reversing lamp (P-03) uses LED light sources, so this time-dependent photometric compliance applies.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only (LED), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the rear position lamp intensities at 1 min and at 30 min (or photometric stability) and verify against the min/max values (e.g. 4 to 17 cd on axis).
requirements.why: The rear position lamp (P-01) is LED-based and falls under 'all other lamps'.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity distribution of the rear position lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, comply at 4 seconds after switch ON, using HV as the reference coordinate.
requirements.test_case: Measure the HV intensity 4 s after switch ON and scale the distribution to verify compliance with the min/max values.
requirements.why: Table A8-1 row 'Front and rear position' applies to rear position lamp P-01.

requirements.text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that all functions are LED-only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements are compliant.
requirements.why: All three lamp functions use LED modules, so compliance at all points in time rests on the paragraph 1.2 results.

requirements.text: In case a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1. to 2.1.3. for the combination of them and checked for compliance.
requirements.test_case: If any function combines LED with another light technology, test at the strictest applicable points in time and verify compliance.
requirements.why: The light-source configuration is to be confirmed, so this conditional applies if mixed technologies are used.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be complied with at all points in time, starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Record the intensity versus time from the Table A8-1 time until stabilisation and verify that the minimum is never undershot.
requirements.why: The LED lamp functions must meet minimum intensities throughout run-up if their run-up behaviour is questioned.

requirements.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure that rear position lamp intensities fall within the steady-intensity category limits.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Conditional failure-mode obligation for the rear position lamp function if it is of category R2.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable), it shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (a)).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the minimum luminous intensity at the test points.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Table 4 row for the R2 variable-intensity rear position lamp, applicable if the lamp is a variable-intensity version.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable) and used as a single lamp, its luminous intensity shall not exceed a maximum of 4.2∙10^1 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the maximum luminous intensity over the light distribution.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Table 4 maximum-intensity limit for the R2 rear position lamp used as a single lamp.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable), it shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (c)).
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at the Figure A3-I grid points and compare with the required percentages.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Table 4 light-distribution requirement for the R2 rear position lamp.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable), it shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (d)).
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity at the boundary of the geometric visibility angles.
